content.text:
### Control transactions with QueryRunner

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/transactions.mdx

Shows how to create a QueryRunner, connect to the database, execute queries, start a transaction, save entities, commit or rollback, and release the query runner. The try/catch/finally ensures rollback on error and release in all cases.

```typescript
// create a new query runner
const queryRunner = dataSource.createQueryRunner()

// establish real database connection using our new query runner
await queryRunner.connect()

// now we can execute any queries on a query runner, for example:
await queryRunner.query("SELECT * FROM users")

// we can also access entity manager that works with connection created by a query runner:
const users = await queryRunner.manager.find(User)

// lets now open a new transaction:
await queryRunner.startTransaction()

try {
    // execute some operations on this transaction:
    await queryRunner.manager.save(user1)
    await queryRunner.manager.save(user2)
    await queryRunner.manager.save(photos)

    // commit transaction now:
    await queryRunner.commitTransaction()
} catch (err) {
    // since we have errors let's rollback changes we made
    await queryRunner.rollbackTransaction()
} finally {
    // you need to release query runner which is manually created:
    await queryRunner.release()
}
```

--------------------------------

### setOnLocked skip_locked

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/query-builder/1-select-query-builder.md

Use setOnLocked("skip_locked") to skip locked rows. Supported on MySQL 8+, Postgres, CockroachDB, SAP HANA.

```typescript
const users = await dataSource
    .getRepository(User)
    .createQueryBuilder("user")
    .setLock("pessimistic_write")
    .setOnLocked("skip_locked")
    .getMany()
```

--------------------------------

### BaseQueryRunner.transactionDepth field semantics

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/packages/typeorm/src/query-runner/BaseQueryRunner.ts

Documents that when transactionDepth > 0, SAVEPOINTs are used to start and commit/rollback transaction blocks. Initialized to 0.

```typescript
/**
 * current depth of transaction.
 * for transactionDepth > 0 will use SAVEPOINT to start and commit/rollback transaction blocks
 */
protected transactionDepth = 0
```

### Faking Migrations and Rollbacks > Transaction modes

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/migrations/08-faking.md

By default, TypeORM will run all your migrations within a single wrapping transaction.
This corresponds to the `--transaction all` flag.
If you require more fine grained transaction control, you can use the `--transaction each` flag to wrap every migration individually, or the `--transaction none` flag to opt out of wrapping the migrations in transactions altogether.

In addition to these flags, you can also override the transaction behavior on a per-migration basis by setting the `transaction` property on the `MigrationInterface` to `true` or `false`. This only works in the `each` or `none` transaction mode.

--------------------------------

### Using CLI > Manage migrations

Source: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/docs/using-cli.md

## Manage migrations

- `typeorm migration:create` - [create](./migrations/03-creating.md) empty migration
- `typeorm migration:generate` - [generate](./migrations/04-generating.md) migration comparing entities with actual database schema
- `typeorm migration:run` - [execute](./migrations/05-executing.md) all migrations
- `typeorm migration:revert` - [revert](./migrations/06-reverting.md) last migration
- `typeorm migration:show` - [list](./migrations/07-status.md) all migrations with their execution status

Learn more about [Migrations](./migrations/01-why.md).
